spec.summary: Sound is half of a Reel or a vlog, and today the editor has one song: a single music file on one track, playing from its offset to the end of the video, plus each video clip’s own sound. Creators layer more than that: a song, a sound effect on a cut, a second song after the first, an ambience bed, a recorded voice. And they need the song to step out of the way when someone speaks, and the finished video to be as loud as YouTube and Instagram expect, so it isn’t turned down or drowned out next to other videos. 208 turns the music track into real **audio tracks**: several tracks, each holding sound clips that are added, moved, trimmed, split and faded like picture clips; **waveforms** on every sound clip and on video clips’ own sound; **volume keyframes** on sound clips (205’s keyframes); **ducking**, which lowers music under speech by measuring how loud the voice tracks are; and a **loudness target** for the export (−14 LUFS for YouTube and Instagram). The preview and the export play the same mix. It is the base 209 (voice-over) records onto.

US-1.text: As a creator making a Reel, I want several sounds on the timeline (two songs, a whoosh on a cut, a crowd ambience), each placed where I want it, so that my video sounds finished.

US-2.text: As an editor, I want to see each clip’s sound as a waveform, so that I can cut on a beat or a word without listening to it over and over.

US-3.text: As a vlogger, I want the music to dip automatically while I talk and come back up when I stop, so that my voice is clear without drawing volume curves by hand.

US-4.text: As a creator, I want my export to be as loud as YouTube and Instagram expect, so that it isn’t turned down or too quiet next to other videos, and never clips.

US-5.text: As an editor, I want to fade, set the volume of and keyframe each sound clip and each track, and undo any of it in one step.

US-6.text: As a keyboard or screen-reader user, I want to add, place and adjust sound clips and tracks, and turn on ducking and the loudness target, without a mouse and hear what changed.

AC-1.text: A project has 1 to 8 audio tracks on web and desktop alike (Q1); the Music track every project has today is the first. Tracks can be added (named “Audio 2”, “Audio 3” …), renamed, reordered among the audio tracks, muted, soloed (Q2), locked and deleted (a track with clips asks first; one undo step). A ninth track, or deleting the last audio track, is refused with the reason. Each audio track has a role, **Music**, **Voice** or **Effects** (Q3): Music for the first and Effects for new ones by default.

AC-2.text: An audio track holds any number of sound clips that don’t overlap, from the files the music takes today (Q4). A sound clip has a start on the timeline, in and out points in its source, a volume from 0 to 200 % (−∞ to +6 dB) and a fade in and fade out of 0 to 10 s each (together not longer than the clip). It is added at the playhead on the chosen track (or the first track with room there; a new track when none has room and there are fewer than 8), and moved, trimmed, split, duplicated and deleted with the timeline’s tools as picture clips are (202: Snap, Slip on its source; Roll, Ripple and Slide within its track, Q5). An edit that would overlap another sound clip on the track, or run past the source’s end, is refused with the reason. Sound past the end of the video is not heard (Q6).

AC-3.text: Migration: a 2.x or 201–207 project’s music becomes one sound clip on the Music track that plays from its offset **to the end of the video** (Q7) with its volume, and its fade-out over the last min(1.5 s, a third of the video), as today. For 201’s to 207’s fixtures the export’s sound sources and gains equal the old ones exactly, and documents without new audio data stay byte-identical when saved.

AC-4.text: Every sound clip and every video clip with sound shows its waveform on the timeline: peaks measured from the decoded sound in the background after import (the import itself is not slower), at least 100 peaks per second of source, scaled by the clip’s volume, fades and volume keyframes so the shape shows what is heard. A trimmed, slipped or sped-up clip (207) shows the part and speed it plays; a clip whose sound is silent (reversed, ramped, a freeze frame, a muted track) shows a flat line and says why on hover and to screen readers. For a fixture of tone bursts at known times and levels, the peaks are within 1 dB and 10 ms of the expected list. Peaks for up to 3 hours of sound per project take under 10 MB.

AC-5.text: A sound clip’s volume can be keyframed with 205’s keyframes (the same diamonds, lane, easing and keys as a video clip’s volume), and each audio track has a volume from 0 to 200 % (Q8). What is heard at any time is the clip’s volume × its fades × its keyframed volume × its track’s volume × ducking (AC-6) × the loudness gain (AC-8), with gain changes smooth (no step longer than 5 ms). For a fixture with every one of these, the export’s gain at 1,000 checked times equals the expected value within 0.01 dB.

AC-6.text: **Ducking** is set per Music or Effects track (off by default, Q9): it lowers that track by an amount (default 12 dB, 3–30 dB) wherever the **voice** is speaking. Voice is the sound of Voice tracks plus the own sound of video and overlay clips (Q10), measured in 50 ms steps; it is speaking where its loudness is above a threshold (default −40 dBFS, −60 to −20), with pauses shorter than 0.5 s bridged so the music doesn’t pump between words. The music fades down over 0.3 s before speech starts and back up over 0.8 s after it stops (Q11). For a fixture with speech at 2.0–5.0 s and 8.0–8.6 s, the ducked track’s gain at every 10 ms equals the expected curve within 0.1 dB; with no voice the gain is unchanged.

AC-7.text: Ducking follows the edit: moving, trimming, muting or changing the volume of a voice clip or track updates the curve within 1 s of the change (measured in the background, never blocking the timeline). The ducking curve is drawn on the ducked track’s clips. The preview and the export apply the same curve, from one function (the one AC-6 checks).

AC-8.text: The export has a **Loudness** setting: Off, YouTube / Instagram −14 LUFS (the default for new projects, Q12), Quiet −16 LUFS, or a value from −24 to −9 LUFS. Loudness is measured as integrated loudness to ITU-R BS.1770-4 / EBU R 128: for EBU Tech 3341 test signals 1–5 (synthesised in the test) the measurement is within 0.1 LU of the expected value. The whole mix is turned up or down by one gain so it measures the target, and peaks are held at or below −1 dBTP true peak by a limiter (Q13): for a fixture mix the exported sound measures the target within 0.5 LU, and no sample exceeds −1 dBTP at 4× oversampling. Off leaves the mix as today. Projects from before 208 keep Off (AC-3).

AC-9.text: The Audio panel shows the mix’s measured loudness and true peak (“−18.4 LUFS, peak −2.1 dBTP; the export will be turned up 4.4 dB”), measured in the background within 2 s of a change for a 60-second project, and says when the limiter will work hard (more than 6 dB of reduction). The preview plays with the same loudness gain as the export (Q14).

AC-10.text: Each change is one undo step: adding, moving, trimming, splitting or deleting a sound clip; a volume or fade drag however long; adding, renaming, reordering, muting, soloing, locking or deleting a track; any ducking or loudness setting. A seeded property test of 1,000 random sound clip, track, ducking and picture edits never leaves overlapping sound clips on a track, a clip outside its source, fades longer than their clip, or more than 8 audio tracks.

AC-11.text: Audio tracks, sound clips, their keyframes, track roles and volumes, ducking and the loudness setting are saved with the project. The document validator clamps volumes, fades, ducking and loudness values to their ranges, drops overlapping or unknown-track clips with the reason, and keeps at most 8 audio tracks; at least 20 malformed documents never make it throw. A project with every case round-trips document → validator → document equal. The sound files themselves are kept as the music is today.

AC-12.text: The export mixes every audible sound clip, video clip sound and track with the gains of AC-5, AC-6 and AC-8, still in 10-second windows interleaved with the frames: memory for sound stays within today’s budget whatever the number of tracks, and for a fixture with 8 tracks the export’s sound sources and gain curves equal the expected list exactly.

AC-13.text: The Audio panel adds sound files (at the playhead, on the chosen track), lists the tracks with their role, volume and ducking, and has the loudness setting with its readout (AC-9). Audio tracks have headers like the others (name, Mute, Solo, Lock, volume, role, ducking) and an **Add audio track** button; sound clips show their name, waveform, fade handles at their top corners and their volume line. The inspector of a selected sound clip has volume, fades, its keyframes and its source. Everything is in the in-app docs.

AC-14.text: Everything in AC-13 works from the keyboard (fade handles and the volume line included, with ← / → and ↑ / ↓, Shift for larger steps); every control has a name and state for screen readers and each change is announced (clip or track, what changed, the new value); axe finds no serious problems in the Audio panel, inspector and timeline; at 360 px wide nothing scrolls sideways outside the timeline.

AC-15.text: Listening test (noted in `specs/testing-strategy.md`): a 60-second vlog with music on the Music track, a voice on a Voice track and two effects is exported with ducking on and −14 LUFS; the music dips under every sentence without pumping between words, nothing clicks at cuts, fades or ducking edges, and the preview sounds the same as the export. YouTube’s “Stats for nerds” shows a content loudness within 1 dB of 0 dB for the uploaded file.

AC-16.text: On the reference mid-range laptop: a 60-second Reel with 4 audio tracks, ducking and the loudness target exports at most 15 % slower than the same Reel with one song and loudness Off; the preview plays it with no more dropped frames than with one song; waveforms of a 10-minute video appear within 10 s of import without dropping preview frames. No regressions: projects without new audio give identical export inputs to 207, and every existing video e2e test passes unchanged.

AC-17.text: `docs/MEDIA-STUDIO.md` (audio tracks, sound clips, waveforms, ducking, loudness, keys, limits), `specs/lld.md` (the audio model, the gain chain, the ducking and loudness measurement), `specs/testing-strategy.md` (the listening test), `CHANGELOG.md` and the in-app docs describe the change; the media studio’s “Still to do” no longer lists several music tracks and clip waveforms.

Q1.text: How many audio tracks? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ up to 8, on web and desktop alike. Mixing is cheap (the export mixes in 10-second windows); the cost is decoding, which grows with clips, not tracks. Reels rarely use more than 4. There is no technical reason to differ by platform (Constitution V), so one limit.

Q2.text: Solo on audio tracks? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ yes, for audio tracks only: soloed tracks are the only audio tracks heard **in the preview** (the export ignores Solo and says so), so the user can check one layer of the mix. The Video and overlay tracks’ sound isn’t soloed in 208.

Q3.text: Track roles: why, and which? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ three roles, Music, Voice and Effects, a simpler form of Premiere’s Essential Sound and Resolve’s Fairlight roles. The role decides what ducking listens to (Voice) and what it can lower (Music, and Effects when turned on). No role-specific processing (EQ, noise removal) in 208.

Q4.text: Which sound files? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ the same as the music today (what the browser decodes: MP3, AAC / M4A, WAV, OGG / Opus, FLAC in Chrome and the desktop app), with today’s size limit per file. Pulling the sound out of a video file as a sound clip (“Extract sound”) is Q15.

Q5.text: Which edit tools work on sound clips? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ select, move, trim, split, duplicate, delete, Snap (to clips, cuts, the playhead and other sound clips), Slip on its source, and Roll / Ripple / Slide within its own track. Magnetic stays the main video track’s only (audio tracks are free like overlay tracks, 203), and sound clips don’t move when the main track ripples, as the music today (Q16 asks about linking).

Q6.text: Sound past the end of the video? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ the video’s length stays set by its pictures and layers; sound clips may run past it on the timeline (drawn dimmed there) but are not heard and don’t lengthen the export. A video made only of sound isn’t possible in 208.

Q7.text: The migrated music, and new songs: fixed length or “to the end of the video”? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ a sound clip has a **Play to the end of the video** switch. Migrated music has it on, so old projects stay identical; a newly added song has it on when it is the first clip on the Music track and is longer than the video, off otherwise. Trimming its end turns it off. Such a clip plays to the end of the video or to the next sound on its track, whichever is first; moved to or past the end, it turns the switch off and keeps the length it had (maintainer, 2026-10-19, T072 option A). Add sound never puts a sound where it would cut such a clip short.

Q8.text: Track volume and pan? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ track volume yes (0–200 %, not keyframed); pan (left / right) not in 208: Reels and Shorts are mostly heard on phones, and pan doubles the mix cases. The loudness target (AC-8) acts as the master volume.

Q9.text: Ducking on by default? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ off for every track, with one **Lower music under voice** switch in the Audio panel that turns ducking on for every Music track at the defaults. On by default would change how old projects sound.

Q10.text: What counts as voice? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ sound on Voice tracks plus the own sound of video and overlay clips (most vlogs talk in the camera clip), with a per-track **Counts as voice** switch to leave a track out (say, a clip with loud music of its own). No speech-recognition model: “speaking” means “louder than the threshold”, so a loud non-speech sound on a voice track ducks too, and the threshold slider is how the user tunes it.

Q11.text: Ducking timing: fixed or adjustable? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ amount and threshold adjustable per track; the fade down (0.3 s, starting before the speech so the first word is clear), the fade up (0.8 s) and the 0.5 s bridging fixed in 208. Most editors expose them, but they are rarely changed and each slider needs explaining.

Q12.text: Loudness target by default? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ −14 LUFS (YouTube’s and Instagram’s reference) for new projects; Off for projects from before 208, so they export exactly as before. YouTube and Instagram turn louder videos down but don’t turn quiet ones up, so a video quieter than −14 just sounds quiet; hitting −14 is the usual advice.

Q13.text: Peaks: a limiter, or only lower the target? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ a true-peak limiter at −1 dBTP (look-ahead 5 ms, release 100 ms), hand-written (no new library, Constitution III), applied after the loudness gain. Without it, turning a quiet mix up to −14 LUFS would clip; lowering the target instead would miss it. The Audio panel warns when it reduces more than 6 dB (AC-9).

Q14.text: Should the preview play at the loudness target? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ yes, with the same gain and limiter, on web and desktop alike, so what the user hears is what they export (Constitution VIII); while a new measurement runs, the last gain is used and the panel says “measuring”.

Q15.text: “Extract sound” (a video clip’s sound onto an audio track as its own clip, to cut picture and sound apart for J and L cuts)? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ not in 208; it changes how clips and their sound are linked and fits better with 210 (compound clips). Video clip sound keeps its volume and keyframes on the clip.

Q16.text: Sound clips linked to a picture clip (moving with it when it ripples)? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ not in 208: sound clips keep their timeline time, as the music does today. Linking is a later feature, with Q15.

Q17.text: Sound for reversed and ramped clips, and same-pitch sound outside 0.5×–2× (left out of 207 “for the audio work”)? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ not in 208; it stays in “Still to do”. 208 is about mixing many sounds, not re-timing one; it can come with 209 or later.

Q18.text: Agent tools (MCP) for audio tracks, ducking and loudness? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-18):_ not in 208; they come with the other timeline tools in 212, like 206’s and 207’s.

sections.title: Non-Functional Requirements
sections.markdown:
- **Performance:** waveforms, ducking and loudness are measured in the background and never block the timeline or the import; the export costs at most 15 % more for 4 tracks with ducking and loudness (AC-16); sound memory stays within today’s budget whatever the number of tracks (AC-12); the entry chunk stays ≤ 350 KB (sound measuring code loads with `import()` when used).
- **Accuracy:** loudness measured to BS.1770-4 within 0.1 LU on EBU Tech 3341 signals, exports within 0.5 LU of the target and ≤ −1 dBTP (AC-8); gains within 0.01 dB of the expected chain (AC-5); ducking within 0.1 dB of its curve (AC-6).
- **What you hear is what you export:** the preview and the export use the same gain chain, ducking curve and loudness gain (AC-5–AC-9, Constitution VIII).
- **Accessibility:** every control works from the keyboard and is announced; waveforms have a text equivalent (clip name, length, whether it is silent and why); axe passes (AC-14).
- **Compatibility:** web and desktop alike; no new dependency (loudness measurement and the limiter are hand-written, Q13); every existing project opens and exports unchanged (AC-3, AC-16).
- **Free and open source:** every audio feature is for everyone, on the web and in the desktop app.

sections.title: Out of Scope
sections.markdown:
- Voice-over recording (209).
- EQ, noise removal, compression other than the output limiter, reverb or other effects; pan (Q8).
- Speech recognition for ducking (voice is measured by loudness, Q10); adjustable duck fade times (Q11).
- “Extract sound” from a video clip, and sound clips linked to picture clips (Q15, Q16).
- Sound for reversed and ramped clips; same-pitch sound outside 0.5×–2× (Q17).
- Sound-only videos; sound lengthening the video (Q6).
- Agent tools for audio (212, Q18).

risks.text: **The preview's Web Audio graph** (§6, D3): `createMediaElementSource` takes an element for good, the context needs a gesture, and the limiter worklet must load under the production CSP and in Electron. Mitigation: a spike task first (worklet module from the Vite build, `app://` origin, autoplay on Play, 207's `preservesPitch` still working through the graph); if the worklet can't load, the preview falls back to a `DynamicsCompressorNode` set as a limiter and says the preview's peaks are approximate (export unchanged).

**Scanning long files** (§3, AC-4, AC-16): a 3-hour video's sound streamed in a Worker may take long and compete with the decoder pool. Mitigation: the scan runs at low priority (one file at a time, yielding between chunks), waveforms fill in as it goes, ducking waits for its voice scans and says "measuring"; measured in 290.

**Loudness accuracy with heavy limiting** (§4, AC-8): one gain then a limiter lands below the target when the limiter works hard. Mitigation: the second, corrective pass when predicted reduction exceeds 1 dB (D4); the panel warns over 6 dB.
**Correlated voices** (§3): the power sum overestimates two copies of the same sound. Mitigation: it only moves the threshold crossing slightly; the threshold slider tunes it; noted in the docs.

**Removing `state.music`** (§7, D1) touches the stage, the timeline, the panel, the export job and tests. Mitigation: one task migrates the store with `projectOf` producing the same `Project` as today (the 201–207 fixtures prove it) before any UI changes.
**Waveforms on every clip** (§9) could slow the timeline at high zoom. Mitigation: canvas per visible bar, columns from the scan by index (no per-sample work), redrawn only on change.

sections.title: Approach
sections.markdown:
Today the sound is two separate things: the video clips' own sound (204's <audio> elements in the preview, \`audioPlan\` + \`mixWindow\` in the export) and **one song** (\`state.music: VMusic\`, its own <audio> element in VideoStage, \`musicClips()\` turning it into one \`AudioClip\` with \`toEnd\`). 208 makes the song an ordinary **sound clip**, lets audio tracks hold many, and puts **one gain chain** in \`engine/\` that the export and the preview both evaluate: clip volume × fades × volume keys × track volume × ducking × loudness gain, then one limiter (Constitution VIII). Under D-033 every task is proven by unit tests; the UI, listening and timing checks go to 290.

**§1 The audio model (\`engine/timeline.ts\`, \`engine/tracks.ts\`, new \`engine/soundClips.ts\`, AC-1–AC-3).** \`AudioClip\` gains \`out\` (source seconds; missing on a \`toEnd\` clip), \`fadeIn\` / \`fadeOut\` (0–10 s, missing = 0), \`keys?: Keyframes<'volume'>\` (205) and \`name\`; \`toEnd\` stays (Q7). \`Track\` gains, for audio tracks only, \`role?: 'music' | 'voice' | 'effects'\`, \`volume?\` (0–2), \`solo?\`, \`voice?: false\` (Counts as voice off, Q10) and \`duck?: { amount, threshold }\` (Q9, Q11); missing fields mean today's behaviour, so old documents stay byte-identical (AC-3). \`TRACK_LIMITS\` audio becomes 8 on web as on desktop (D2). \`tracks.ts\` gets \`addAudioTrack\` ("Audio N", role Effects, placed after the last audio track), and \`moveTrack\` / \`deleteTrack\` learn audio tracks (reorder only among audio tracks; the last one can't go). \`soundClips.ts\` holds the pure sound clip edits: \`addSound\` (at the playhead on the chosen track, else the first with room, else a new track below 8), \`moveSound\`, \`trimSound\`, \`splitSound\`, \`duplicateSound\`, \`deleteSound\`, \`slipSound\`, \`rollSound\`, \`rippleSound\`, \`slideSound\`, \`setFades\` — each refusing overlaps on the track, running past the source, fades longer than the clip, and locked tracks with the reason, as 202's edits do; Snap targets gain sound clip edges (\`timeSnap.ts\`). A sound clip's length is \`out − in\`, or for \`toEnd\` the video's end minus its start (capped by the source). Trimming a \`toEnd\` clip's end turns \`toEnd\` off (Q7). Sound past the video's end is cut by \`audioPlan\`, never lengthening \`projectLength\` (Q6).

**§2 The gain chain (\`engine/soundPlan.ts\`, \`engine/keyframes.ts\`, new \`engine/mixGain.ts\`, AC-5, AC-12).** \`SoundSource\` gains \`track\` and \`role\`; \`audioPlan\` emits every sound clip of every unmuted audio track (with its fades, keys and \`toEnd\` fade-out of min(1.5 s, a third), exactly as today for migrated music) after the clip sounds, in track order, so a project without new audio yields exactly 207's list (AC-3). \`mixGain.ts\` is the one place the chain is evaluated: \`sourceGainAt\` (today's: keys or volume × edges × fades) × \`trackGain\` (track volume) × \`duckGain\` (§3) — with sound clip volume keys on a 0–2 range (\`SOUND_RANGES\`; video clips stay 0–1, D6). \`gainCurve\` keeps its 5 ms step, so every change is a ramp of at most 5 ms (AC-5). The loudness gain and the limiter (§4) act on the summed mix, after the chain.

**§3 Waveforms, voice and ducking (new \`engine/soundScan.ts\`, \`engine/ducking.ts\`, new \`state/soundScan.ts\` + \`state/soundScan.worker.ts\`, AC-4, AC-6, AC-7).** Each media file with sound is **scanned once** in the background (D5): a module Worker streams its sound through Mediabunny's \`AudioBufferSink\` (as the export does, so a 3-hour file is never decoded whole) and \`soundScan.ts\` folds the samples into a \`SoundScan\`: peaks (max |sample|, 100 per second, as Uint8 dB steps) for the waveform and RMS in 50 ms steps (Float32, dBFS) for voice detection. 3 hours = 1.08 M peaks + 216 k RMS ≈ 2 MB (< 10 MB, AC-4). Scans are kept per media id in memory and dropped with the media. **Waveforms** are drawn from the scan through the clip's mapping (\`sourceAt\` for video clips at speed, 207) and scaled by \`mixGain\` at each column; silent clips (\`soundMuted\`, muted tracks) draw flat with the reason as their title. **Voice** on the timeline is computed, not measured again: for each 50 ms step, the power sum of every voice source's scanned RMS × its chain gain (without ducking) at that time (\`voiceLevel(plan, scans, step)\`); **speaking** = above the track's threshold, pauses < 0.5 s bridged; \`duckCurve(speaking, amount)\` ramps down over 0.3 s *before* speech (look-ahead: we know the future) and up over 0.8 s after, as dB, sampled every 10 ms. Because it reads cached scans only, an edit's new curve takes milliseconds (AC-7's 1 s), and the export and the preview call the same \`duckGain(curve, time)\`. The curve is cached per (project sound edit, scans) and recomputed on change.

**§4 Loudness and the limiter (new \`engine/loudness.ts\`, \`engine/limiter.ts\`, AC-8, AC-9).** \`loudness.ts\` is BS.1770-4: the K-weighting filters (the standard's two biquads at 48 kHz), 400 ms blocks with 75 % overlap, the −70 LUFS absolute and −10 LU relative gates, channel weights 1.0 for L / R, and true peak by 4× oversampling (the standard's 48-tap polyphase FIR); a streaming \`LoudnessMeter\` takes window after window. \`limiter.ts\` is a streaming true-peak limiter: 5 ms look-ahead, instant attack to hold the oversampled peak at −1 dBTP, 100 ms release, state carried across windows (Q13). **Measuring the mix** (\`measureMix(job)\` in \`videoExport.ts\`, sharing \`mixWindow\`): render the mix window by window (sound only, no pictures), feed the meter, keep nothing else. The loudness gain is \`target − measured\` (clamped to ±24 dB); when that gain plus the measured true peak goes over −1 dBTP by more than 1 dB, a second pass measures *with* gain and limiter and corrects the gain once, so heavy limiting still lands within 0.5 LU (D4). **The panel readout** (AC-9) runs \`measureMix\` in the background 500 ms after the last sound edit (cancelled by the next), and stores \`{ key, lufs, peak, gain, reduction }\` keyed by a hash of the sound plan; **the export** reuses it when its key matches, else measures first ("Measuring loudness…"). Loudness Off: no gain, no limiter, the mix exactly as today.

**§5 The export (\`engine/videoExport.ts\`, \`state/videoExportJob.ts\`, AC-12).** \`ExportJob\` carries the sound clips with their files (\`ExportAudio\` already has a file), the tracks' audio fields, the duck curves and the loudness gain. \`mixWindow\` schedules each source's gain as one \`setValueCurveAtTime\` of the full chain (\`gainCurve\` over \`mixGain\`), then the window's output (still 10 s, interleaved with the frames, so memory is the same whatever the number of tracks) passes through the loudness gain and the streaming limiter before \`SoundFeed\` adds it; the limiter's 5 ms delay is compensated by starting the mix 5 ms early and flushing at the end, so sound stays on the frame.

**§6 The preview (\`components/studio/previewSound.ts\`, \`VideoStage.tsx\`, D3, AC-7, AC-9).** Element volume can't go over 1 or carry curves, so the preview routes its <audio> elements through **one \`AudioContext\`**: each element → \`MediaElementAudioSourceNode\` → its gain (the chain from \`mixGain\`, set each tick with a ≤ 1-frame ramp) → the master gain (loudness gain) → an \`AudioWorkletNode\` running \`limiter.ts\` → the speakers. \`soundPlan\` (preview) learns sound clips: those under the playhead on unmuted (and, when any is soloed, soloed) audio tracks play, the next within 2 s are loaded, as video clip sound is today; the music's separate element in VideoStage goes. Solo is preview-only (Q2). The context is resumed on Play (a user gesture). The worklet loads from a same-origin module URL (CSP \`script-src 'self'\` covers worklets; a spike proves it in the production build and Electron, risk 1).

**§7 State and undo (\`state/videoStore.ts\`, new \`state/videoSound.ts\`, \`state/videoMedia.ts\`, \`state/videoTracks.ts\`, AC-10).** \`state.music\` becomes \`state.sounds: VSound[]\` (an \`AudioClip\` with its \`file\`, \`url\` and media id, D1) and \`projectOf\` passes them as \`audio\`; \`state.loudness\` (\`'off' | number\`) and the per-track fields live on \`tracks\`. \`videoSound.ts\` has the actions (\`addSoundFiles\`, \`moveSound\`, \`trimSound\`, \`splitSound\`, \`duplicateSound\`, \`deleteSound\`, \`setSoundVolume\`, \`setSoundFades\`, \`setTrackVolume\`, \`setTrackRole\`, \`setDucking\`, \`setLowerMusicUnderVoice\`, \`setLoudness\`), each one \`change()\` with a coalescing key so a drag is one step; \`updateMusic\` (not recorded for undo today) goes. \`setMusicFile\` becomes \`addSoundFiles\` (same formats and 100 MB limit, Q4) and starts the scan instead of \`measurePeaks\`; video imports start a scan too. A seeded property test runs 1,000 random sound clip, track, ducking and picture edits and checks AC-10's invariants after each.

**§8 Saving (\`engine/projectDoc.ts\`, \`engine/projectGate.ts\`, AC-3, AC-11).** \`toDocument\` writes the new fields only when set; \`readAudio\` reads \`out\`, fades, keys and \`name\` (clamped; overlapping clips on a track dropped with the reason, later one first to go), \`readTracks\` the audio fields and keeps at most 8 audio tracks; the document's \`loudness\` is read with its range, missing = Off (Q12: pre-208 projects stay Off; new projects start at −14 in the store). 2.x documents go through \`fromSequence\` as today.

**§9 UI (\`VideoPanels.tsx\` → new \`AudioPanel.tsx\`, new \`SoundRow.tsx\`, \`TrackHead.tsx\`, \`ClipInspector.tsx\` → new \`SoundInspector.tsx\`, \`PictureRow.tsx\`, \`Timeline.tsx\`, \`36-media-studio.css\`, AC-13, AC-14).** The Audio panel: Add sound (several files), the tracks (role, volume, ducking), **Lower music under voice**, the Loudness setting and readout with the limiter warning. Audio track headers: name, Mute, Solo, Lock, volume, role, ducking; **Add audio track**. \`SoundRow\` replaces \`MusicRow\`: one bar per sound clip with name, waveform canvas, fade handles at its top corners, the volume line, the ducking curve, dimmed past the video's end; drag, trim and the edit tools go through \`timelineDrag.ts\` as picture clips do. Video clips draw their waveform under the filmstrip. The sound clip inspector: volume (0–200 %), fades, its volume keyframes (205's \`KeyframeButton\` / lane), Play to the end of the video, source. Pure helpers (waveform columns, bar geometry, announcements) are unit-tested; the UI is checked in 290.

sections.title: Data Structures & Interfaces
Techniques
sections.markdown:
- **One chain, two players.** `chainGainAt` is the only place gains are multiplied; the export samples it into `setValueCurveAtTime` (5 ms steps), the preview sets it each tick. `limiter.ts` is plain TypeScript run by the export directly and by the preview's worklet, so both limit alike.
- **Scan once, compute the rest.** Waveforms, voice level and ducking read the per-file scan; nothing is decoded again for an edit. Voice level is a power sum of scaled RMS (sources assumed uncorrelated, which a voice under music is); loudness is measured on the real mix, not estimated (D4).
- **BS.1770-4 to the letter**, tested against EBU Tech 3341 signals 1–5 synthesised in the test (stereo 1 kHz sines and the gating cases): integrated within 0.1 LU, true peak by the standard's 4× polyphase FIR.
- **Streaming everything:** the scanner, `measureMix`, the meter and the limiter take one chunk or window at a time with state carried, so memory is per window, never per project (AC-12).
- **Old projects untouched:** missing fields mean today's behaviour; `audioPlan` lists clip sounds first as today; Loudness Off skips the gain and limiter, so 201–207 fixtures give bit-identical export inputs (AC-3, AC-16).
- **Announcements** through the timeline's live region, as 202–207 do ("Audio 2: Whoosh, fade in 0.5 s").
- **No new dependency** (Constitution III): Mediabunny (already used) decodes; filters, meter, limiter and FIR are ~400 lines of our own.

sections.title: Decisions for the maintainer (accepted 2026-10-18: D1–D6 as recommended)
sections.markdown:
- **D1 — The song becomes a sound clip.** `state.music: VMusic` is replaced by `state.sounds: VSound[]`; the music's own <audio> element, `musicClips()`, `updateMusic` and `MusicRow` go. *Recommended*: one model for every sound; the alternative (keeping `music` beside a new list) doubles every rule.
- **D2 — 8 audio tracks on the web too.** `TRACK_LIMITS` has 4 sound tracks on the web today (201); the spec (Q1) says 8 everywhere. Audio tracks cost no decoders by themselves (the videos-at-once limit still bounds video clips). *Recommended*: raise the web to 8; picture tracks stay 4 / 8.
- **D3 — The preview through Web Audio.** Clip and sound elements go through one `AudioContext` (gains, master, limiter worklet) instead of `element.volume`, which can't pass 100 % or follow the duck curve exactly. *Recommended*; spike first (risk 1).
- **D4 — Loudness measured on the real mix.** A sound-only pass before the export (or the panel's background measurement when still valid), plus one corrective pass only when the limiter would reduce more than 1 dB. *Recommended*: exact and cheap next to encoding pictures; the alternative (estimating from per-file scans) can be off by several LU for correlated sounds.
- **D5 — One background scan per file**, in a module Worker, streamed with Mediabunny: peaks (100 / s) and 50 ms RMS, kept in memory per media id (not saved). *Recommended*; ducking and waveforms then cost no decoding per edit.
- **D6 — Volume ranges.** Sound clips 0–200 % (with keys on 0–2); video clips' own sound stays 0–100 % as today (205 Q8). *Recommended*: the spec only asks 200 % for sound clips; widening video clips can come with "Extract sound" (Q15).
